thread:
devon: Heads-up — yesterday's aggregate backfill for `agg_hours` spawned duplicate replays for ~120 tenants. Noticed by dashboard freshness alerts this morning.

jess: Ugh. Any idea why? did quota checks fail? :thinking_face:

devon: Looking at the job-run logs: scheduler enqueued the same shard window twice. There's a race between the console "Start backfill" flow and the replay-queue consumer that ignores `reservation_id` on retries.

mike: Can you paste the log snippet?

devon: Sure:
```
INFO 2026-03-18 02:14:03 scheduler - created replay job shard=eu-12 window=2026-03-15T00:00/2026-03-15T01:00 reservation_id=none
INFO 2026-03-18 02:14:05 console-api - user triggered backfill tenant=acct-42 reservation_id=abc123
INFO 2026-03-18 02:14:05 scheduler - created replay job shard=eu-12 window=2026-03-15T00:00/2026-03-15T01:00 reservation_id=none
```

anya: So the scheduler created a job before console reservation was attached, then when console retried it created another. Both ended up running because the replay consumer treats reservation_id as metadata only.

leo: That explains duplicates. We should enforce idempotency at enqueue time. Either attach reservation_id early, or dedupe by (shard, window, tenant).

jess: Agreed. Short-term: can we add an enqueue-time check that rejects if an in-flight job exists for same (shard, window, tenant)? Long-term: console should reserve before scheduler can see the window.

mike: Short-term sounds safest. But watch out for race if two consoles request start at the same millisecond. Use a DB upsert with (shard, window, tenant) unique key and a state enum {reserved, queued, running}. If upsert finds existing -> return existing reservation id.

devon: I'll draft a small patch to scheduler: on create => do upsert into replay_reservations; if returns existing reservation_id, skip creating duplicate job and return that id. That should cut duplicates to zero for this class.

anya: Also need to patch the replay consumer to honor reservation_id: if reservation_id doesn't match the reservation table state (e.g., already consumed by another job), bail and mark as deduped. Safer than just running and relying on eventual dedupe.

jess: Can we also add a console UX hint? Right now the console shows "Backfill started" the moment user confirms even if scheduler hasn't reserved. That misleads users into thinking a reservation is guaranteed. We should show "Reserving..." + spinner until reservation confirmed.

leo: +1. Analytics: instrument counts for "reservation_attempts", "reservation_conflicts", and "duplicate_runs_prevented". We need numbers for SRE runbook and to validate fix.

mike: For the DB approach, prefer to use the existing metastore (Postgres) rather than adding redis. Keep TTL on reservations so stale reservations don't block forever: set expiry to 48h and a background sweep to clear orphaned reservations once job completes.

devon: I'll open a PR for scheduler + consumer changes. Plan: patch -> canary to staging -> 24h guarded window on prod. Any objections?

anya: No objections. Ops ask: hold all new large-scale backfills until we cut the hotfix in prod. We already saw a spike in S3 egress because duplicates reprocessed heavy logs.

jess: Noted. I'll add a console banner: "Backfill runs paused until replay reservation hotfix is deployed" and disable the start button for non-admins.

replay-bot: [automation] Replay job queue length dropped from 392 -> 48 after paused runs. Current dedupe prevented ~118 duplicate jobs.

mike: Thanks. Devon, assign me to review the PR. Also add a tiny integration test that simulates simultaneous console + scheduler enqueues to validate upsert dedupe.

devon: Will do. PR link when ready. For the postmortem, let's capture root cause: console optimistic UI + scheduler create-before-reserve race + consumer ignoring reservation state. Action items: short-term upsert guard, consumer check, console UX change, metrics.

jess: I'll create the incident doc and tick the action items into the eng-platform backlog. :memo:

anya: One more note — ensure we don't silently drop legitimate replays that need to run after a cancellation. Reservation lifecycle needs careful state transitions (reserved -> queued -> running -> done/cancelled). We'll document that in the migration notes.

devon: Good catch. We'll include state machine and migration plan in the PR description.

leo: Great. Thanks everyone.
